clue.text: Idiot missing half of proclamation in parliament

indicators.note: missing half of the call means only its front half is kept and the rest dropped

parts.note: a group of owls is a parliament, and the call a tawny owl proclaims is ...-twoo

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a garbled announcement made in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parliament' looks political, but it is the collective noun for owls, so their proclamation is the call twit-twoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a silly, foolish person is called a twit in casual British speech.

clue.text: Language spoken on the other side of the world is music to Eliza's ears

definitions.text: Language spoken on the other side of the world

indicators.note: Eliza Doolittle of My Fair Lady speaks Cockney, so the word is said with her accent

parts.note: a strain is a passage of music or a tune

explanation.surface: Australian speech sounds lovely to the heroine of My Fair Lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle, the Cockney flower girl in My Fair Lady, would pronounce 'strain' with the vowel the answer spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian English, the slang name being a jokey rendering of 'Australian' in a broad accent; Australia is on the opposite side of the globe from Britain.

clue.text: Triple disc may be purchased with this?

indicators.note: may be signals that these letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A three-CD set might be bought with this voucher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' makes TRIPLE DISC into an anagram; the definition 'purchased with this' describes the answer as something goods are bought with.
explanation.definitionFit: A store voucher given in place of a refund can be spent on goods in that shop.

clue.text: Agent's player after flying start

indicators.note: after places the player behind the opening letter
the start of the word flying is its opening letter

parts.note: an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A talent agent's performer gets off to a flying start.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a factor is someone who acts as an agent buying or selling goods for another.

clue.text: Soft inland turtle

indicators.note: the word in, split off the front of inland, places the soft letter within the land

parts.note: terrain is land or ground
p, for piano, means soft in music

explanation.surface: A gentle freshwater turtle found away from the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'inland' into 'in' and 'land': P (piano, soft) goes inside TERRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, an example of the wider category.

clue.text: Rising thus: Shrek?

indicators.note: in a down light, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, thus

explanation.surface: A rising argument: does it follow that this is Shrek?
explanation.definitionFit: Shrek, the green hero of the animated films, is an example of a monster, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Yoko hugged by Harry, promoting 11 as a mark of respect

indicators.note: hugged by means Yoko's surname is held inside the other name
11 across is THIRD, so the third letter of the name is promoted, moved up to second place

parts.note: taken as written
Yoko Ono, the artist married to John Lennon

explanation.surface: Yoko Ono is embraced by a Harry who honours her.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 across is THIRD, so 'promoting 11' lifts the third letter of the name one place up the column before Yoko's surname goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorary title or degree is conferred as a tribute, without the usual requirements or duties.

clue.text: Eighty percent included? That's kind

indicators.note: included signals letters held within the words eighty percent

explanation.surface: Is eighty percent counted in? That would be generous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective meaning generous, but here it is the noun meaning sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a type is a sort or category, as in 'a kind of thing'.

clue.text: Scandal in the sluice

definitions.meaning: the political affair that brought down President Nixon in 1974
a gate controlling a flow of water, as in a sluice

explanation.surface: A scandal is uncovered in the sluice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Washington building that gave its name to Nixon's scandal; literally a floodgate or sluice gate.

clue.text: Blloody triumph

parts.note: bloody means gory, and the clue's spelling has an extra L inside it, so gory gains an L in the same place

explanation.surface: A bloody victory, with a deliberate typo.
explanation.walkthrough: The misspelling is the wordplay: BLOODY is GORY, and the stray L added to 'Bloody' is added to GORY too.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: glory is triumph or the honour won by a great victory.

clue.text: Spreading dirt around hospital is what 2 need to become 12

indicators.note: around puts the shuffled letters round the hospital sign
spreading the dirt about rearranges its letters

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Muck smeared around a hospital is what a couple need to make a group of three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spreading' rearranges DIRT into TIRD; 'around' wraps it round H. The definition: a twosome needs one more person, a third, to become a threesome (12 across).
explanation.definitionFit: An extra person, the one who joins a pair; a couple plus one more makes a group of three.

clue.text: Trinity Hall, reading electrical engineering, student starts delving into book

indicators.note: delving into puts the run of letters inside the book

parts.note: a tome is a large book
H is an abbreviation for hall
R stands for reading, one of the three Rs
EE is the usual abbreviation for electrical engineering

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of student

explanation.surface: A student at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, reads electrical engineering and digs into a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trinity Hall' looks like the Cambridge college, but it splits into the definition and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a trinity is a group of three, as is a set of three people.

clue.text: Speaker's dainty half-sister

parts.note: twee means excessively dainty or quaint

indicators.note: half here means the back three letters of the six-letter word sister

explanation.surface: The speaker's pretty younger half-sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-sister' looks like a family relation; it is half of SISTER, its last three letters TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is a small loudspeaker unit that reproduces high-pitched sound.

clue.text: A fraction in temporary accommodation hotel

parts.note: a tent is a shelter put up for a short stay
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Only some of the guests are in tents at a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: one part of something divided into ten equal parts is one such fraction.

clue.text: Previous Egyptian spy that Iran got the covers off

indicators.note: covers off means each word loses its outer letters, keeping only its insides

explanation.surface: An earlier Egyptian agent whom Iran exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers off' strips the first and last letters from each of spy, that, Iran, got and the, leaving P, HA, RA, O, H.
explanation.definitionFit: The rulers of ancient Egypt bore this title, so a ruler from Egypt's past.

clue.text: Play acting out in a 3-D picture

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of play acting are put out of order

explanation.surface: Performing a play outdoors in a stereoscopic picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to an anaglyph, a picture printed in two colours that looks three-dimensional through tinted glasses.

clue.text: Individual involved with soldier can become malnourished

indicators.note: can become signals that two sets of letters together rearrange to make the word malnourished

explanation.surface: A person who gets mixed up with the army can end up underfed.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus SOLDIER ('involved with') shuffled would give MALNOURISHED; take SOLDIER's letters out and HUMAN remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an individual person is a member of mankind, a person.

clue.text: Setback for Lebanon, having lost an illustrious prize

indicators.note: setback means the word is set going backwards
having lost means the word an is taken out of Lebanon

explanation.surface: A blow to Lebanon, missing out on a great award.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove AN from LEBANON to get LEBON; 'Setback' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known example of a famous award, given annually for peace, literature and science.

clue.text: Ceremony heard in good French city

indicators.note: in puts the sounded ceremony inside the French word

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: heard means the word for ceremony is used by its sound, giving a homophone

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A ceremony is heard in a fine French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French city' wants to be the definition, but 'good French' is BON and the definition is just 'city': BRIGHTON is on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an English seaside city on the south coast of Sussex.

clue.text: Person in command of isle appears regularly in magazines

indicators.note: in signals letters sitting within the word command

explanation.surface: Someone who runs an island turns up often in magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: Layered: also 'isle' (the Isle of Man) and the 1st, 4th and 7th letters of 'magazines'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a person, an adult human, especially a male one.

clue.text: An experience of women, archetypically

indicators.note: of signals the answer is formed from letters running across the words women archetypically

explanation.surface: Something every woman goes through, as a classic example.
explanation.definitionFit: The first menstrual period is an experience in the life of every woman, typically in puberty.

clue.text: In Siberia, by small crevasse

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is held inside the run of words siberia by small

explanation.surface: A deep crevasse beside a small spot in Siberia.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic synonym: an abysm is an abyss, a deep chasm.

clue.text: Bend 8 for accessory

definitions.meaning: 8 down is TYPE, so this is a type of bend: a very tight one doubling back on itself
a pin worn to keep hair in place

explanation.surface: A kind of bend serves as a fashion accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp U-shaped bend in a road; also a U-shaped pin for holding hair.

clue.text: Greenware from fancy lace fellow (incidentally also here in the absence of conflict)

indicators.note: fancy suggests the letters of lace are elaborately rearranged

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: Pottery made from ornate lace and a man, with a theme aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is a theme note: take WAR ('conflict') from GREENWARE and GREENE remains, the novelist whose titles fill this grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Celadon is a pale green glazed pottery from China and Korea, a kind of greenware.

clue.text: This diplomat needs to have dined at his place of work

indicators.note: needs to have means the diplomat lacks the eaten part, which must be added to make his office

parts.note: a consulate is the office where a ... works
ate means dined

explanation.surface: A diplomat should eat lunch at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as a sum: the diplomat plus ATE (dined) makes his office, CONSULATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is a government official posted abroad to protect citizens and trade, a kind of envoy.

clue.text: Because of abbey's location being unfinished?

indicators.note: unfinished means the place name loses its last letter

parts.note: Downton Abbey is the TV period drama, set at Downton

explanation.surface: Why the abbey site is incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: Downton Abbey is a British TV drama about an aristocratic family; cut its final N.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: owing to something, or attributable to it, as in 'it's all thanks to you'.

clue.text: Fish and rabbit order: parents do it

parts.note: a school is a group of fish swimming together
Run, Rabbit, Run is the old wartime song, so run is an order to a rabbit

explanation.surface: Fish and rabbit dishes ordered by parents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run, Rabbit, Run' is a British wartime music-hall song. The definition: parents drive children to and from lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: The daily trip taking children to classes and collecting them is something mothers and fathers do.

clue.text: Break pots?

parts.note: ... turned ..., upside down in a down light, gives the clue's word pots

explanation.surface: Smash the pots?
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a short stay or break in a journey.

clue.text: See 24
Might prisoner meet the Queen?

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Could a prisoner get to meet the Queen?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb, but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: might is strength or force.

clue.text: Lull to sleep with this music

definitions.meaning: to sway a baby gently back and forth
a loud, guitar-led genre of popular music

explanation.surface: Use this music to send a baby off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway a cradle gently, which lulls a child; also a style of popular music.

clue.text: Layer oddly, ounce after ounce

indicators.note: after places the odd letters behind the abbreviation
oddly means the odd letters, first third and fifth, of ounce

explanation.surface: An odd layer, one ounce added to another.
explanation.definitionFit: The ozone layer is the band in the stratosphere that absorbs ultraviolet rays.

clue.text: The obscenely rich use it as a rule of thumb, perhaps

indicators.note: obscenely suggests the letters are twisted in an outrageous way

explanation.surface: The very wealthy use it as a rough guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A heuristic is a practical method or shortcut for problem-solving rather than a strict procedure.
